title: 3rd Sitting of First session of 2026
summary: After the opening prayers, attendance and agenda, the Majlis approved the minutes of the first two special sittings held outside the session and referred the President's nominations of non-resident ambassadors (including the United States, Cuba, Oman and Armenia) to the Foreign Relations Committee. The main business was the preliminary debate on an opposition member's bill to make damaging mosques a terrorism offence, which every speaker backed while ruling-party and opposition members traded sharp political criticism. After a 30-minute recess a second, government-sponsored National Service bill was introduced but nobody signed up to debate it. The terrorism amendment was accepted 56 to 0 and sent to the Committee on Security Services. Attendance figures at the start are read from garbled digits; 59 members were present for the vote.

items.title: Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: Chair read out the figures (digits garbled in the text)

items.title: Approval of minutes of the first and second special sittings of 2026 held outside the session
items.outcome: Accepted by the chair; no amendments filed

items.title: Announcements from the chair: committee membership change on the independent institutions committee
items.outcome: A PNC member of the committee was replaced by the member for North Hithadhoo

items.title: Matters from the Speaker's desk: President's nominations of non-resident ambassadors to the United States, Cuba, the Commonwealth, Brazil, Mexico, Oman and Armenia
items.outcome: Each referred to the Foreign Relations Committee under rule 124

items.title: Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Counter-Terrorism Act (Law 2015/32), sponsored by the member for North Galolhu
Preliminary debate on the National Service Bill, sponsored by the government through the member for South Kulhudhuffushi
items.outcome: Bill presented; debate interrupted after recess with no speakers signed up

items.title: Vote on accepting the Counter-Terrorism Act amendment bill
items.outcome: Accepted 56-0; referred to the Committee on Security Services

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Backed the bill and said the ruling group would pass it at committee stage, while criticising opposition conduct and past governments' record on mosques.
Exchanged remarks with the chair and opposition members over language used across the floor, including the label 'irreligious'.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Fully backed the amendment and urged quick committee work, while disputing government claims about how many mosques it had built.
Raised a point of order objecting to remarks he said were untrue, made by members across the floor.
Said the bill already had cross-party support and should not turn into a party fight; noted mosque promises in his area.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Called the bill important, regretted that few members spoke for it, and said no party's love of Islam should be questioned.
Said the bill makes mosque damage a clear offence and that no one should be labelled irreligious.
Urged members to speak truthfully and questioned claims about what $18 million of mosque funding could build.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Introduced his bill to list damage to mosques as a terrorism offence, arguing mosques should be protected and offenders face firm penalties.
On a point of order, asked members to stop calling one another irreligious across the floor.

speakers.name: Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the amendment, said Maldivians value mosques and Islamic rites, and pointed to government religious programmes including plans for Ramadan.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported the bill, said the heaviest penalty should be written into law, and cautioned against party labelling and rhetoric that may endanger people.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Supported the amendment and raised complaints from mosque cleaners about harassment and job threats linked to the Malé City Council.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Supported the bill, credited the current government with building mosques and creating an Islamic ministry, and sharply criticised the opposition over corruption.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the amendment, said mosques should not be politicised, and urged faster government development projects in his constituency.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill, said attacks on mosques may stem from illness, and favoured moving mosque management from councils to the Islamic Ministry.

speakers.name: Qasim Ibrahim
positions: Backed protecting mosques but said existing general laws already allow punishment; spoke about government debt and the dollar rate.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Said mosque damage is unacceptable but existing laws already allow action, so better enforcement matters more than this amendment.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill, welcomed opposition recognition of past mistakes, and tied mosque protection to Islam's core aims of protecting religion, life and property.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the amendment, asked why it was not brought earlier when its sponsor's party held power, and praised the new zakat law.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Supported the bill, credited the government with rebuilding mosques, and criticised raising such issues just before local council elections.

speakers.name: Faruhath Mohamed
positions: Presented the government's National Service Bill, a structured national service programme for young people with training, benefits and rules for participants.

decisions: Minutes of the first and second special sittings of 2026 were accepted as adopted.
Nominations for non-resident ambassadors to the US, Cuba, Brazil, Mexico, Oman, Armenia and the Commonwealth were referred to the Foreign Relations Committee.
A PNC member of the independent institutions committee was replaced by the member for North Hithadhoo.
The Counter-Terrorism Act amendment bill was accepted at preliminary stage and referred to the Committee on Security Services.
Debate on the National Service Bill was interrupted with no speakers signed up.

votes.what: Accepting the bill to amend the Counter-Terrorism Act (Law 2015/32), 59 present, 29 needed
